question: In which of the following organisms is fragmentation common?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only a few multicellular organisms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fragmentation is a type of asexual reproduction common in certain multicellular organisms.
 
• It is especially prevalent among organisms such as sponges, some annelid worms, and sea stars.
 
• During fragmentation, an organism breaks into fragments, each capable of growing independently into a new organism.
 
• This method allows rapid population expansion in favorable conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asexual Reproduction**

 
 
• It is a mode of reproduction where offspring arise from a single organism.
 
• It does not involve the fusion of gametes, and the offspring are genetically identical to the parent.
 
• Common methods include binary fission, budding, fragmentation, and spore formation.
 
 
 
• **Binary Fission**
 
 
• A form of asexual reproduction most commonly observed in prokaryotic organisms like bacteria.
 
• The parent organism divides into two equal-sized daughter cells.
 
 
 
• **Budding**
 
 
• Another form of asexual reproduction where a new organism develops from an outgrowth or bud due to cell division at one particular site.
 
• It is commonly seen in yeast and some invertebrates like hydra.
 
 
 
• **Spore Formation**
 
 
• Involves the formation of spores that can develop into new individuals.
 
• Commonly observed in fungi, algae, and some plants.
